title: Sonar debt limitations
summary: Rule remediation costs are useful input, not a complete project-debt measure.

sections.label: Verified definition
sections.text: Sonar’s technical-debt metric uses remediation costs associated with detected rules. It does not measure every architectural, data, requirements, or workflow problem.

sections.label: Proposed practice
sections.text: Use rule findings as evidence to investigate. Protect new code through appropriate quality gates and improve existing debt incrementally. Do not equate a displayed remediation estimate with a calibrated delivery estimate.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Prioritized findings have actual impact, owner, evidence, and verification beyond the rule label.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow steps: Investigate the cause, Recommend go or no-go, Tests and review. These links are recommendations based on the guide content, not required product or process choices.
A metric note names the actual Sonar product, configured rules, analyzed revision, exclusions and displayed remediation estimate.
Triage links each accepted finding to an observed consequence and owner rather than relying on the rule label or metric total.
The verification packet records the agreed quality gate and meaningful behavior evidence. Sonar remediation time is not substituted for delivery effort or total project debt.
Existing source claims were not re-audited in this mapping pass. Project configuration, usefulness and actual check outcomes remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use this Sonar example when a displayed remediation cost or technical debt figure is about to be read as the project's whole debt or as a delivery estimate. It explains what the metric covers and how to use rule findings as evidence to investigate.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
